verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The market empties out and the pigeons take the square.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Cold stones remember
every footstep that passed here—
now only wingbeats.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A shutter clatters
somewhere down an empty street—
dusk collects its coins.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone left a lamp on
in a room above the shops—
light doesn't know yet
that the day is finished.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Moths find the window,
tap their small persistent hopes—
the lamp keeps burning.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone should tell them
the hand that lit it is gone—
still, the glass stays warm.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Warmth outlasts the reason
for its being lit at all—
the moths don't need one.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I forgot to ask
whether the lamp burned for me
or just happened to.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Either way I stayed,
circling what I couldn't name—
call that light enough.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Enough to keep me
from asking what enough means—
the wax already spent.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Someone else must strike
the next match, blind in the dark—
I've forgotten how.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I'll find the matchbox
by the shape of its absence—
my hands still remember.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Then strike it for me—
let the small flame answer back
whatever I forgot.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I'll hold the light still—
watch how it leans toward your hand
before you even ask.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the flame doesn't ask
who lit it, only leans there—
warm, unbothered, sure

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the wax runs downward
never once asking permission—
this is how it stays lit
